annotation.authors_or_issuer: 立法院 (Legislative Yuan of Taiwan), 李淑瓊
key_provisions_or_claims: Taiwan Civil Code Art. 191-1 and Consumer Protection Act Arts. 7-9 fit poorly with autonomous learning robots due to causation and supply-chain complexity.
Opaque decision-making creates evidentiary difficulties for victims.
Discusses new legal category or AI personhood, noting risk of weakening human accountability.
EU AI Liability Directive proposed 2022; Commission planned withdrawal in 2025 work programme.
Recommends balancing consumers and supply chain and evaluating amending laws or a special statute.
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Legislative Yuan research brief on product liability for smart robots in Taiwan. It examines Civil Code and Consumer Protection Act limits for autonomous, learning robots, discusses legal personhood and the EU AI Liability Directive, and recommends evaluating statutory amendments or a special law balancing consumers and supply-chain actors.
annotation.title_clean: 智慧機器人之產品責任問題研析
annotation.title_en: Analysis of Product Liability Issues for Smart Robots
annotation.venue: 立法院議題研析 (Legislative Yuan issue analysis)
